summary: A standalone, lighter roll-and-write-style spinoff of Rajas of the Ganges that keeps the same race-to-intersect-money-and-fame idea but strips it down to shared dice and pencil-and-paper-style province building. It plays faster and simpler than the original, aimed at a broader, more casual audience.
praised: Faster, more accessible than the original
Keeps the clever crossing-tracks win condition
Good for introducing non-gamers to the family
criticised: Less depth than the base game
Feels like a simplified reskin rather than its own thing

interaction.kind: shared dice drafting, mostly parallel play
interaction.detail: Players draft from a shared pool of rolled dice each round but then develop their own paper province independently; interaction is limited to competing over which dice to take.

subsystems: goods market trading (selling goods → money, escalating value per kind sold)
river/karma track progression (bonuses and tie-break resource)
sources: fame from connecting buildings (1-3 points depending on upgrade)
money from selling goods when a market is connected (up to 3 at once, escalating value)
money from the Trader palace action (sell up to 2 goods)
bonus symbols on tracks/province edges (fame or money)
karma track (used only as a tiebreaker, not itself scored)
scoring.how_you_win: As in the parent game, you fill in your pad to push a fame track and a money track toward each other from opposite ends; the moment one player's fame and money entries intersect, the round is finished out and whoever's tracks cross the intersection point by the most wins (ties broken by karma collected/used).
scoring.score_note: race: win when fame/money markers meet

_name: Rajas of the Ganges: The Dice Charmers
